item.title: Japanese Yen sticks to intraday gains amid reviving safe-haven demand, intervention fears
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) remains on the front foot against a retreating US Dollar (USD) and draws support from a combination of factors.

item.title: United Arab Emirates Gold price today: Gold rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices rose in United Arab Emirates on Monday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: Gold climbs to record high near $4,400 on safe-haven flows
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) rises to an all-time high near $4,300 during the early European trading hours on Monday. The precious metal gains momentum on the expectation of US Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate cuts after signs of softer US inflation and cooler jobs reports.

item.title: Pound Sterling Price News and Forecast: GBP/USD rises ahead of the UK’s third-quarter GDP release
item.description: GBP/USD gains ground after three days of losses, trading around 1.3390 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair depreciates as the Pound Sterling (GBP) holds ground ahead of the release of the United Kingdom (UK) Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for the third quarter.

item.title: GBP/JPY trades with negative bias below 211.00/multi-year peak amid modest JPY strength
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross kicks off the new week on a softer note and erodes a part of Friday's strong gains to a fresh high since August 2008 – levels just above the 211.00 mark.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Remains above 1.1700 as bullish momentum builds
item.description: EUR/USD breaks its four-day losing streak, trading around 1.1720 during the Asian hours on Monday. On the daily chart, technical analysis indicates a prevailing bullish bias, as the pair remains slightly above the ascending channel pattern.

item.title: EUR/GBP softens below 0.8750 ahead of UK GDP release
item.description: The EUR/GBP cross attracts some sellers to around 0.8745 during the early European session on Monday.

item.title: USD/INR holds last week’s gains-driven by RBI’s double intervention
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) holds onto last week’s gains against the US Dollar (USD) at the start of the week. The USD/INR pair clings to losses near 90.00, driven by the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) intervention in the spot and non-deliverable forward (NDF) market to support the Indian Rupee.
